A perpetual software licensing fee discount if the vendor fails to meet international color standards.

explanation: A legally binding Service Level Agreement (SLA) establishing strict remediation timelines (e.g., critical blocker fixes within 15–30 days, high severity within 60 days) holds the vendor accountable for accessibility defects discovered during the contract term, with defined financial penalties or termination rights for non-compliance.

distractorNotes.a: Non-disclosure agreements restrict communication and do not create any obligation for the vendor to remediate defects.
distractorNotes.c: Verbal informal agreements are legally unenforceable and provide no assurance of timely remediation.
distractorNotes.d: Fee discounts without mandatory remediation terms leave barriers unresolved for users with disabilities.

sourceNote: W3C WAI procurement guidance recommends formal contract terms with SLAs defining remediation timeframes by severity.

stem: Why should an enterprise include a "Right to Audit" and independent verification clause in accessibility procurement contracts?

options.text: To permit the customer to inspect proprietary backend source code repositories for security backdoors.
To allow the customer to install unlicensed copies of the vendor software across all employee laptops.
To validate vendor ACR claims through independent technical testing before issuing final payment.
To require the vendor to reimburse all hardware upgrade costs incurred by the customer IT department.

explanation: A "Right to Audit" clause gives the procuring organization the legal right to conduct independent accessibility verification (or hire a third-party auditor) on the vendor deliverables before accepting the software or releasing milestone payments, verifying that the vendor ACR claims match actual software performance.

distractorNotes.a: Software security auditing clauses are distinct from accessibility conformance verification rights.
distractorNotes.b: Right to audit does not grant unauthorized software licensing privileges or duplicate distribution rights.
distractorNotes.d: Hardware depreciation and IT infrastructure costs are separate from software accessibility compliance verification.

sourceNote: W3C WAI procurement guidelines advise incorporating independent audit rights prior to software acceptance.

stem: Under European Standard EN 301 549, which chapter governs the accessibility requirements for downloadable electronic non-web documents, such as PDF and Word reports?

options.text: Chapter 4 (Functional performance statements for biometric identification systems).
Chapter 6 (Two-way voice communication and real-time text frequency requirements).
Chapter 9 (Web content and internet-hosted browser-rendered applications).
Chapter 10 (Non-web documents including downloadable electronic office files).

explanation: EN 301 549 Chapter 10 applies WCAG Success Criteria (Level A and AA) to non-web documents, including downloadable document formats like PDF, Microsoft Word, and spreadsheets. Chapter 9 applies to Web content, Chapter 11 applies to Software, and Chapter 12 applies to Documentation and Support Services.

distractorNotes.a: Chapter 4 defines overarching functional performance statements across ICT rather than document requirements.
distractorNotes.b: Chapter 6 covers two-way voice communication and real-time text (RTT), not electronic documents.
distractorNotes.c: Chapter 9 applies specifically to web pages and browser-based web applications, not non-web documents.

sourceNote: EN 301 549 Chapter 10 defines accessibility requirements for non-web documents including PDF and office files.

stem: In EN 301 549 Chapter 11 (Software), how are WCAG success criteria adapted for non-web desktop and mobile software?

options.text: Criteria are adapted by substituting terms like "software" for "web page" and addressing platform APIs.
All WCAG criteria are replaced by proprietary operating system accessibility guidelines and patents.
Software is evaluated exclusively against contrast rules while keyboard access requirements are waived.
Native software applications are automatically exempt if distributed through certified digital app stores.

explanation: Chapter 11 of EN 301 549 adapts WCAG 2.1 success criteria for software applications (both open and closed). It maps web concepts to software equivalents (e.g., replacing "web page" with "software program" or "unit of software") and adds requirements for interoperability with platform accessibility services (such as accessibility APIs).

distractorNotes.b: EN 301 549 is an open European standard that harmonizes directly with WCAG rather than relying on proprietary vendor patents.
distractorNotes.c: Chapter 11 includes comprehensive requirements for keyboard operability, focus, and assistive technology API integration.
distractorNotes.d: App store distribution does not grant exemption from EN 301 549 statutory procurement compliance requirements.

sourceNote: EN 301 549 Chapter 11 adapts WCAG success criteria for software programs and platform accessibility services.

stem: When evaluating an enterprise software procurement under EN 301 549, what technical requirements are established in Chapter 12?

options.text: Requirements governing physical wheelchair ramp dimensions at vendor corporate headquarters.
Requirements ensuring product documentation and technical support services are fully accessible.
Requirements mandating that all software engineering source code be released under copyleft terms.
Requirements setting maximum hardware processor temperatures and cooling fan acoustic decibels.

explanation: EN 301 549 Chapter 12 specifies requirements for "Documentation and support services". Clause 12.1 covers product documentation (user guides, manuals, and online help must be provided in accessible formats), and Clause 12.2 covers support services (help desks, chat, phone support must accommodate the communication needs of individuals with disabilities).

distractorNotes.a: Physical building architecture and wheelchair ramps fall under building codes, not EN 301 549 ICT standards.
distractorNotes.c: Software licensing models (such as copyleft or open source) are not governed by accessibility technical standards.
distractorNotes.d: Hardware thermal and acoustic engineering parameters are not part of Chapter 12 documentation and support requirements.

sourceNote: EN 301 549 Chapter 12 mandates accessible product documentation and accessible technical support services.

stem: A procurement officer reviews an ACR submitted by a vendor in 2026. The report is titled "VPAT Version 1.0 (US Section 508)". Why should this ACR be rejected?

options.text: Because VPAT Version 1.0 requires payment of international patent licensing royalties to the US government.
Because Version 1.0 reports can only be processed using deprecated 16-bit mainframe computer operating systems.
Because it evaluates obsolete 2000 Section 508 standards rather than the Revised Section 508 based on WCAG.
Because all procurement reports submitted after 2020 must be written exclusively in the German language.

explanation: VPAT 1.0 evaluated the legacy US Section 508 standards from 2000. In 2017/2018, the US Access Board refreshed Section 508 to incorporate WCAG 2.0 Level AA. ITI subsequently released VPAT 2.x. Submitting a VPAT 1.0 in 2026 means the vendor evaluated against obsolete standards and failed to evaluate modern WCAG criteria.

distractorNotes.a: VPAT templates are freely provided by ITI and do not involve patent licensing royalties or government fees.
distractorNotes.b: VPATs are standard text or PDF documents and have no technical dependency on legacy 16-bit computer systems.
distractorNotes.d: Language requirements depend on the procuring entity and jurisdiction; international English VPATs are standard.

sourceNote: Section508.gov warns against using outdated VPAT 1.0 templates that do not reflect the Revised 508 WCAG standards.

stem: Under an Accessible Procurement Maturity Model, which factor best demonstrates that a prospective vendor has high organizational maturity in web accessibility?

options.text: The vendor advertises an automated one-line JavaScript overlay widget that modifies client web stylesheets.
The vendor offers a substantial marketing discount if the customer agrees to waive all accessibility testing.
The vendor promises that an external contractor will fix all reported accessibility bugs within five years.
The vendor has an internal accessibility team, automated CI/CD checks, and publishes transparent ACR updates.

explanation: High accessibility maturity in a vendor organization is evidenced by institutionalized processes: dedicated accessibility subject-matter experts, automated regression testing integrated into CI/CD pipelines, accessible design system components, regular employee training, and transparent, regularly updated Accessibility Conformance Reports.

distractorNotes.a: One-line overlay widgets are superficial band-aids that do not remediate underlying code or indicate vendor maturity.
distractorNotes.b: Offering discounts to waive accessibility testing represents low maturity and high risk of non-compliance.
distractorNotes.c: Relying on external contractors with a five-year turnaround indicates an ad-hoc, reactive, and immature capability.

sourceNote: W3C WAI procurement maturity emphasizes institutionalized vendor processes, internal expertise, and transparent ACRs.
